text:
sam: Seeing a weird scheduling pileup in us-west-2: ~40 pending pods that request fractional GPUs (we use device-plugin that exposes nvidia.com/gpu) but cluster-autoscaler isn't adding new nodes. Pods are Pending with "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" even though there are spare GPU slots on mixed instance types.

alex: Can you paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pending pods?

sam: Sure, here's one:```Name: batch-infer-4d7c
Pod IP: <none>
Nodes: <none>
Labels: app=batch-infer, tier=batch
Containers:
  infer
    Image: repo/infer:latest
    Limits:
      cpu: 4
      memory: 12Gi
      nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25
    Requests:
      cpu: 2
      memory: 8Gi
      nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler   0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.```

maria: Ah, fractional GPU requests — we're on a mixed fleet with g5s and g4dn instances. Device plugin advertises whole GPUs only, and our scheduler fragmentation is because kube-scheduler doesn't binpack fractional GPU across nodes. CA refuses to scale because nodes exist with free GPU capacity but not whole GPUs for the request.

leo: Is the request actually using device-plugin fractional counts or do we convert to device plugin count? I thought we had a custom webhook that rounds up to 1 GPU for limits.

sam: No rounding for these batch jobs — they intentionally request 0.25 gpus to permit share. The device plugin advertises `nvidia.com/gpu` as an integer capacity and the Kube scheduler treats the resource as scalar, so 0.25 works for scheduling only if multiple fractional pods fit on a single node's integer GPUs. We're hitting fragmentation: some nodes have 1 free GPU each but already host pods claiming 0.5, so a new 0.25 can't be scheduled because of binpack fragmentation with discrete allocation.

alex: CA logs? infra-bot, do we have recent cluster-autoscaler events for that nodepool?

infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler[controller] 2026-03-17T16:02:09Z: Found 2 unschedulable pods; scale-up not needed: there are nodes with sufficient resources (but unschedulable due to PodTolerations/Taints mismatch).

maria: There are also anti-affinity rules and a `nodeSelector` for instance-type family on these pods; they only target the `gpu-shared` pool. Some older nodes in that pool are tainted `gpu.dedicated=true:NoSchedule` for dedicated workloads — these batch pods don't tolerate it. CA refuses to provision other pools because the pods are constrained to that pool.

leo: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) relax nodeSelector for batch windows, or 2) add a small helper DaemonSet that exposes fractional gpu shard pooling (we once tested a GPU-sharing sidecar), or 3) change webhook to round fractional requests up to 1 GPU so CA will add nodes with full GPUs instead of leaving fragmentation.

sam: Short-term I vote for (1) — relax nodeSelector for jobs queue for next 2 hours so CA can scale other pools with spare capacity. Long-term we should evaluate MPS or MIG slicing per-node so we can host fractional across hardware uniformly.

alex: Also check kubelet reserved and device-plugin registration: some g5 nodes are registering GPUs as `nvidia.com/gpu:0` due to driver crash, so CA sees capacity but scheduler can't place. Run: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}\n{end}'`

sam: Ran that, output:```g5-1 1
g5-2 1
g4-1 1
g4-2 1
gpu-old-1 0
gpu-old-2 0``` Two old nodes show 0 because driver didn't register. I've cordoned them.

maria: After cordon, CA will try to replace them if nodepool uses autoscaling group. But CA still stuck due to pod tolerations and nodeSelector as said. I can patch the Job controller to remove nodeSelector for the next 2 hours.

leo: Also add a small scheduler extender? Might be overkill. For now, patch jobs, and add a temporary admission webhook to bump 0.25 -> 1 for any job with `batch-infer` label, until we implement MIG profiles.

alex: Agree. One more thing: set `--scale-down-unneeded-time` low for the burst window so we don't keep excess nodes for too long.

sam: I'll patch the job controller now and roll the change to the queues. Rolling update in progress... :spinner:

infra-bot: Deploy: job-controller v2.4.1 promoted to staging at 2026-03-17T16:08:41Z by maria

maria: Patch applied to queue; new pods are scheduling on g5-2 and g4-1. We'll monitor costs.

leo: For backlog: open ticket to explore MIG (per-GPU slice) vs MPS with benchmarking on g5s. Also evaluate a small admission webhook that can opportunistically pack fractional requests into node pools with a lightweight packing heuristic.

alex: Nice. Add a follow-up to infra board and tag @platform for capacity planning. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all — the queue drained in ~12m after changes. Leaving cordon on old nodes until we deprovision them.

maria: Filing postmortem notes in incidents channel with remediation timeline.

leo: :tada:
